headline: Cyclone Arnab forms over Bay: four maritime ports on signal 2
summary: The storm is expected to intensify into a very severe cyclonic storm before crossing India's Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday.
details: A deep depression in the Bay of Bengal has intensified into Cyclone Arnab. It is forecast to strengthen further and cross India's Andhra Pradesh coast as a very severe cyclonic storm on Wednesday.
As of 6:00 am today, the storm was located 820 km southwest of Chattogram port, 745 km southwest of Cox's Bazar port, 785 km south of Mongla port, and 745 km south of Payra port.
The maximum sustained wind speed within 54 km of the center is approximately 62 km/h, with gusts reaching up to 88 km/h.
The Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) has instructed the maritime ports of Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla, and Payra to hoist distant warning signal No 2.
Fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay of Bengal have been advised to remain close to the coast and navigate with caution.
Meteorologist Abdul Hamid Mia of the BMD stated that Cyclone Arnab is not expected to have a significant impact on Bangladesh, though coastal areas may see light rain tomorrow and the following day.
After the cyclone makes landfall in India, Dhaka and Rajshahi divisions may also experience light rain.
The storm's name, 'Arnab', meaning 'sea' or 'ocean', was proposed by Bangladesh as part of a regional naming system involving 13 countries.
Cyclones are classified into five categories based on wind speed: cyclonic storm, severe cyclonic storm, very severe cyclonic storm, extremely severe cyclonic storm, and super cyclonic storm.
caption:
A new cyclone has formed in the Bay of Bengal. Four maritime ports are now on signal 2 as it heads toward India.

A deep depression in the Bay of Bengal has intensified into Cyclone Arnab. It is forecast to strengthen further and cross India's Andhra Pradesh coast as a very severe cyclonic storm on Wednesday.

As of 6:00 am today, the storm was located 820 km southwest of Chattogram port, 745 km southwest of Cox's Bazar port, 785 km south of Mongla port, and 745 km south of Payra port.

The maximum sustained wind speed within 54 km of the center is approximately 62 km/h, with gusts reaching up to 88 km/h.

The Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) has instructed the maritime ports of Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla, and Payra to hoist distant warning signal No 2.

Fishing boats and trawlers in the North Bay of Bengal have been advised to remain close to the coast and navigate with caution.

Meteorologist Abdul Hamid Mia of the BMD stated that Cyclone Arnab is not expected to have a significant impact on Bangladesh, though coastal areas may see light rain tomorrow and the following day.

After the cyclone makes landfall in India, Dhaka and Rajshahi divisions may also experience light rain.

The storm's name, 'Arnab', meaning 'sea' or 'ocean', was proposed by Bangladesh as part of a regional naming system involving 13 countries.

Cyclones are classified into five categories based on wind speed: cyclonic storm, severe cyclonic storm, very severe cyclonic storm, extremely severe cyclonic storm, and super cyclonic storm.

headline_marked: Police HQ [[denies extrajudicial killings]] after IGP's 'crossfire' remark
headline: Police HQ denies extrajudicial killings after IGP's 'crossfire' remark
summary: The Police Headquarters clarified that IGP Ali Hossain Fakir used the term 'crossfire' to emphasize law enforcement strictness, not to suggest killings outside the legal process.
details: Police Headquarters issued a clarification on Monday evening following widespread criticism of Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir's statement that police would use 'crossfire' if permitted by the government.

The HQ stated that the IGP used the term 'crossfire' literally to express a firm commitment to taking effective action against drug traffickers, terrorists, and extortionists who threaten public safety.
The clarification explicitly denied that the term was used to refer to extrajudicial killings or the punishment of individuals outside of the judicial process.

Police HQ highlighted that officers often face direct attacks and violence while performing their duties, citing that 176 attacks on police occurred in the first 10 months of 2026, leaving four officers dead and 370 seriously injured.

The statement further emphasized that police actions are governed by the laws of the land, including the right to self-defense under the Penal Code 1860, the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, and the Police Act 1861.
Additionally, the HQ addressed confusion regarding the IGP's comments about journalists, stating that any negative remarks were unintentional and occurred accidentally.
The controversy sparked reactions from Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) and other critics who called the IGP's remarks a 'dangerous signal' and demanded accountability.
